Toy Case Towards designing an extractor satisfying the above three properties, we first consider an alternate task. Instead of poly(d(λ))-copies of the log(d(λ))-qubit state |ψ⟩, we are given all the amplitudes of |ψ⟩, say (α1 , . . . , αd(λ) ), in the clear. Can we extract true randomness from this? For instance, we could extract b1 , . . . , bd(λ) , where bi is the first bit of the real component of αi . Firstly, it is not even clear that bi is distributed to according to the uniform distribution over {0, 1}. Moreover, all the bits b1 , . . . , bd(λ) are not independent and in fact, are correlated with each other due to the normalization condition i |αi |2 = 1. P Fortunately, we can rely upon a result in random matrix theory [24], that states the following: suppose (α1 , . . . , αd(λ) ) are drawn from a Haar measure in S(Rd ) then it holds that any o(d(λ)) co-ordinates of (α1 , . . . , αd(λ) ) are 1/o(d(λ))-close in total variation distance with o(d(λ))-dimensional vector where each component is drawn from i.i.d Gaussian N (0, d1 ).
